Subject: Re: Production — sudden spike in 504s and request latency

Quick technical summary from runtime investigation:

What we observed:
- Starting 07:47 PDT we see continuous rounds of request fan-out from the front-tier for many short-lived sessions. Instead of coalescing into steady batches, requests are being broken into very small batches (~1-3) and then reissued.
- This correlates with rapid prefix-cache regeneration for a hot keyspace (approx 12k prefixes), where the cache eviction/repop flow triggers synchronous KV reloads on miss.
- The combination leads to queueing at the GPU worker queue: while KV reloads occur, new requests pile up and exceed the request time budget -> 504s.
- We also see retry amplification from the SDK: client retries are triggering new request floods, because the short batches are perceived as timeouts.

Root cause hypothesis:
- A recent change to the batching policy (aggressive latency-first thresholds) plus a subtle cache invalidation race caused a hot prefix to be evicted and then regenerated repeatedly under load. The regeneration path is synchronous and blocks the worker thread rather than using background warm-population.

Mitigation applied (11:30 PDT):
- Forced the routing layer to route Crestline traffic to a warm pool with cache pinned (fallback variant).
- Temporarily disabled the newest batching-latency optimization on affected nodes (roll back patch).
- Enabled background async prefix warm-population so KV misses do not block serving threads.

Next steps:
- We’ll push a patch to make cache repopulation async + cap concurrent repopulations per node (PR attached: batching-policy-override.patch).
- Postmortem and throttling suggestions for long-term: tune back the aggressive batching windows, implement per-prefix regen rate-limits, and add an early circuit for retry storms.

Attachments: crestline_network_traces.zip (netflow), batching-policy-override.patch

Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Update: Crestline incident — mitigation completed, next steps

Grace —

Thanks for your patience. Update and summary of actions taken: 

1) Impact window: 07:47–11:28 PDT on 2027-04-30. During that time your /generate endpoints saw elevated 504s and high tail latency (peak 14% 504s).
2) Root cause (short): a batching-latency policy change plus synchronous prefix-cache repopulation created a regeneration storm for a hot keyspace that led to GPU worker queueing and amplified client retries.
3) Immediate mitigations applied: routing to warm-pinned model variant, rollback of the batching policy, enabled async cache warm-population, and rate-limit on prefix repopulation. These actions restored normal error rates by 11:28 PDT.
4) Follow-ups we’ll deliver by 2027-05-04:
   - Full RCA document with timeline and logs (shared Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/crestline-incident-20270430)
   - Patch to make repopulation async and cap concurrency (PR linked to RED-2198).
   - Post-incident review and recommended batching defaults for enterprise customers.

We also attached the network traces and a sample error log for your records. As Marissa noted, we’re prepared to offer a one-month service credit provisionally; we’ll finalize once RCA is published.

If you’d like a 30-minute exec review with our leadership, we’re available today at 14:30 PDT — please let us know what works.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
